newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary c.bank sees no foreign borrowing this year.
newsitem.headline: Hungary c.bank sees no foreign borrowing this year.

text.p: The National Bank of Hungary (NBH) said on Wednesday it does not expect to tap foreign bond markets for the remainder of this year.
"It is not likely that the NBH will take up more foreign loans this year," NBH President Gyorgy Suranyi told a news conference.
The NBH earlier said it might borrow abroad this year to set a new benchmark for Hungarian issues, but only if the conditions were better than for previous Hungarian bonds. @
The NBH took up a $350 million syndicated loan in July. The loan had five years' maturity and an interest of 0.5 percent over LIBOR.
Suranyi said the NBH will not need further foreign loans until the end of 1997, adding that the bank could still tap the foreign markets next year.
"If we do that, it will be with improved conditions and with the purpose of creating a better benchmark for the foreign borrowing of Hungarian business," he said.
